title: Buildings bought by City grantees: the deed, the loans and the City’s paper
question: When a nonprofit bought a building with City money, did the purchase close before the City approved the money, and how was it paid for in between?
finding: 1044 Howard Street: the deed to United Playaz was recorded on 2022-12-07 (document 2022109688), 69 days before the Board's vote, with same-day deeds of trust to a private trust; COMMUNITY VISION CAPITAL & CON. The housing office's first recorded document followed on 2023-06-23 (fixture filing / declaration of cc&r to SFCC-MAYORS OFFICE OF HOUSING & COMMUNITY DEV), the same day a deed of trust was reconveyed. 758 Pacific Avenue went from a private trust to Chinatown Community Development Center in 2023 and to its partnership, New Asia Housing, in 2024, which the City then agreed to buy it from.
how: For each grantee purchase: the latest deed to a party other than the City, deeds of trust recorded the same day, the first later document naming the City, the housing office or the Housing Accelerator Fund, and any reconveyance recorded that day. The Board vote date for 1044 Howard Street is taken from the case file.
limits: Buying first with a bridge or seller loan and repaying it from public money later is a standard way to close a sale on time, and the Board can authorize reimbursement. The index gives no amounts: what the seller-held loan was, and how much City money paid it off, need the deeds and the grant agreement. A reconveyance the same day suggests, but does not prove, a payoff.
